proposed_comments.title: Refresh frame metrics before preserving the client crop

confidence.rationale: The pinned upstream path changes the target to WS_CHILD, then reads client geometry without a frame refresh and later adds the already-applied diffX/diffY offset again. The converged fork correction builds successfully; exact-upstream and isolated-candidate builds were attempted but dependency restoration blocked them, and runtime UI execution was unavailable.

proposed_comments.body:
### Refresh frame metrics before preserving the client crop

**Severity:** `high`

After `SetParent` and `WS_CHILD` are applied, the code immediately measures `GetWindowRect`/`GetClientRect`. The frame metrics can still describe the pre-style-change frame, so the calculated non-client dimensions do not reliably preserve the original client area. The final `x`/`y` calculation also adds `cropRect`, which was already shifted by `diffX`/`diffY` above, and therefore applies that client-origin offset twice.

Please force a no-size `SetWindowPos` with `SWP_FRAMECHANGED` immediately after `SetWindowLongPtrW` and before the `GetClientRect` measurement. Then calculate the final child offset from the measured client origin while subtracting the earlier `diffX`/`diffY` conversion from `cropRect` (for both axes). Verify the maximized-browser case and retain the existing non-maximized reparent coverage.

Focused verification: build the CropAndLock UI test project and run the maximized and non-maximized reparent scenarios when the Windows UI test environment is available; confirm the visible pixels and input hit-testing use the same selected client region.
